- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted values.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment median as anchor for correction.
